scope: Independent CPU-only production renderer/gesture audit. No browser, GPU, full-domain or GMAT rerun.

findings.effect: F focusCraft changes camera while the active ray-based apsis drag remains; a subsequent pointer event can use a different projection.
findings.fix: Cancel an active new orbit gesture before camera focus/axis/reset changes, or disable such changes while held.
findings.test: cancels an active ray-constrained edit before the F focus command changes its camera
findings.resolution: Root cancels active new orbit gestures before focusCraft, viewAxis, flyCamera, setMode and resize camera/projection changes.

findings.effect: render still advances tween and calls OrbitControls.update while controls.enabled=false; the disabled flag alone does not establish camera immutability.
findings.nextEvidence: Check right-orbit then immediate handle drag and drag during a camera transition, with actual browser camera/plan observations.
findings.resolution: Actual onDown clears tween/follow without moving the current camera; render suppresses controls.update while the new drag is held and resumes normal updates after cleanup.

limitations: Label rasterization and native pointer hit testing are not covered by the CPU constructor-free scene tests.
Main closure transaction rollback was source-reviewed; the CPU lifecycle test covers GameScene callback order rather than a browser-held UI transaction.
Seven passing cases repeated in the rejection batch are not seven additional unique tests.
No publication, performance or commercial-quality conclusion follows from this audit.

The ninth case invokes production onDown/render with a sentinel controls.update callback. It establishes the guard and camera invariance in CPU execution, not real native OrbitControls damping behavior.
